DATA FORMATS

CSV to JSON converter

Convert CSV to JSON or JSON to CSV with explicit headers, delimiters and type options. Read a local UTF-8 file, inspect the result, then copy or download it in your browser.

Local files & pasted text

Up to 1 million UTF-16 code units. UTF-8 files up to 2 MB. Nothing is uploaded.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to convert CSV to JSON

Paste CSV or open a local file. Choose a delimiter, decide whether the first row contains headers and select Convert. Leave type inference off to retain every field as a string. Switch modes to turn an array of JSON objects or arrays into CSV.

CSV records ↔ JSON objects or array rows

References: CSV conventions: RFC 4180 · Papa Parse documentation · OWASP: spreadsheet formula injection

Good to know

Will identifiers keep their leading zeros?

Yes. CSV input defaults to strings: 001 stays "001", an empty cell stays "", and large IDs remain text. Optional type inference recognizes exact true, false, null and JSON-number syntax. Leading-zero numbers and values with surrounding spaces remain strings. Unsafe or non-finite numeric values also remain strings; decimals use JavaScript number precision.

How do headers and uneven rows work?

With headers enabled, the first record supplies nonempty, unique, case-sensitive object keys. Duplicate or blank headers are rejected. Headerless input produces arrays. All rows must have the same number of fields; missing and extra fields produce an error. Header spaces and cell whitespace are preserved. Skip empty rows removes records whose cells are all empty, not whitespace-only records.

Which delimiters and quoted fields work?

Auto detection considers comma, tab, semicolon and pipe. If detection is inconclusive, comma is used and the result explains that choice. Choose the delimiter explicitly for ambiguous files. Quoted fields may contain delimiters and newlines; escape a quote by doubling it. Bare quotes and malformed quoted fields are rejected. One final record terminator does not create an extra row.

What JSON shape can be exported as CSV?

Use an array of objects or an array of equal-length arrays. Object headers use the union of keys in first-seen order. Missing keys and null become empty cells; CSV cannot preserve that distinction from an empty string. Nested objects and arrays are rejected unless Serialize nested values as JSON is enabled. Array rows do not receive generated headers. An empty array downloads as an empty file.

What does spreadsheet formula protection change?

In JSON to CSV mode, protection is on by default. String cells starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return receive a leading apostrophe, including headers. The status shows how many changed. Actual numeric negative values remain numeric text. Turn protection off when exact original string values are required. CSV quoting alone does not prevent spreadsheet formulas; different spreadsheet import settings can behave differently.

What are the limits and line endings?

Input is limited to 1,000,000 UTF-16 code units; UTF-8 files to 2 MB; tables to 10,000 data records and 200 columns. JSON documents also have an 80-level and 50,000-value/field limit. Output is limited to 3,000,000 characters. CSV output quotes every cell and offers CRLF or LF record endings. An initial UTF-8 BOM is removed. Files and conversion input stay in browser memory.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Keep a record’s meaning explicit

CSV has fields, but no built-in number, boolean or null types. Select the interpretation that fits your destination.

CSV fieldDefault JSONWith type inference
001"001""001"
42"42"42
true"true"true
null"null"null
Empty cell""""
9007199254740993Exact stringExact string; unsafe as a number

A comma inside a name belongs inside double quotes: 002,"Lin, Mei",false has three fields. A quote inside a quoted field is doubled. This is structural conversion, not automatic repair of broken exports. For configuration documents, use YAML ↔ JSON. To decode a string containing a JSON document, use JSON unescape.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Nested JSON: a string cell or an expanded table?

Choose the intended shape before exporting. Preserving an object inside one cell is a different transformation from expanding its fields into columns.

For a complete example, choose JSON to CSV, paste the input below, enable Serialize nested values as JSON and select Convert to CSV. The id remains a string. The customer object and tags array are each stored as JSON text in one CSV cell.

[{"id":"001","customer":{"name":"Ada"},"tags":["red","blue"]}]

With object headers, comma delimiter and the default CRLF record ending, the result is:

"id","customer","tags"
"001","{""name"":""Ada""}","[""red"",""blue""]"

The doubled quotes belong to CSV escaping. Parsing this CSV with string values produces a customer string containing {"name":"Ada"}, not an automatically restored object. See JSON strings and encoding layers for how representations differ.

GoalResult shapeCurrent tool
Preserve nested valuesOne row; customer and tags each occupy one cellSupported with nested serialization enabled
Expand object fieldsA customer.name column containing AdaRequires a separate flattening transformation
Expand array itemsTwo rows, one per tag, repeating the parent idRequires a defined array-expansion policy

Arrays can multiply row counts; missing fields, empty arrays and identical path names also need explicit rules. This converter does not guess those rules or automatically flatten objects. Files are read one at a time, with the limits above. JSONL output and multi-file merging are outside the current format options.
